metadata.goal: Analyze characteristic patterns and variations in recurring urban mobility.
metadata.category: Multi-user recurring and occasional Montréal trajectories with route families, destinations, land-use, purpose, departure period, mode, GPS positions, and point speeds.
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 22 Recurring Route Speed Destination Patterns
metadata.dataset_description: Multi-user recurring and occasional Montréal trajectories with route families, destinations, land-use, purpose, departure period, mode, GPS positions, and point speeds.
metadata.metric_note: Distances and directness are calculated from delivered GPS polylines; point speeds, trip durations, chain timing, and paired-leg timing are synchronized with the supplied point table. Route directness ratio is route distance divided by straight-line distance, so it is at least 1 and lower values indicate more direct routes.

plot.title: Recurring-route Speed Profiles
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How similar are point-level speed profiles across uses of the same recurring route?
insight_list.insight: Recurring routes generally preserve similar speed profiles, especially during the middle portions of trips.

plot.title: Peak-period Motor-vehicle Speed Disruption
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do motor-vehicle speed fluctuation and lower-tail speed vary with rush-period proximity overall, and does the pattern persist within recurring route families?
insight_list.insight: Motor-vehicle trips departing closer to peak periods show larger speed fluctuations and lower lower-tail speeds, even along repeatedly used routes.

plot.title: Employment and Mixed-use Recurrence
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do recurring employment and mixed-use trips differ in weekday concentration, mode consistency, purpose, and departure time?
insight_list.insight: Recurring trips to employment areas are more concentrated on weekdays and use consistent transportation modes, while repeated trips to mixed-use areas span more purposes and departure times.

plot.title: Recurring Concentration and Occasional Diversity
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: At equal trip sample sizes, how do recurring and occasional trips differ in destination and purpose diversity?
insight_list.insight: Across users, recurring trips concentrate on a small set of destinations, while occasional trips account for most spatial and purpose diversity.

insights: Recurring routes generally preserve similar speed profiles, especially during the middle portions of trips.
Motor-vehicle trips departing closer to peak periods show larger speed fluctuations and lower lower-tail speeds, even along repeatedly used routes.
Recurring trips to employment areas are more concentrated on weekdays and use consistent transportation modes, while repeated trips to mixed-use areas span more purposes and departure times.
Across users, recurring trips concentrate on a small set of destinations, while occasional trips account for most spatial and purpose diversity.
summary: Repeated routes retain recognizable middle-trip speed shapes. Peak motor-vehicle repeats contain more disruption, employment recurrence is weekday- and mode-consistent, and occasional trips provide most of the destination and purpose diversity.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this controlled constructed dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
